title: Development of a method for the detection of zinc in Brassica oleracea using solid phase extraction and size-exclusion chromatography inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (SEC-ICP-MS)
author: Dell'Aquila

steps.title: Cook, freeze-dry, and grind vegetables
steps.instruction: Purchase savoy cabbage, broccoli, and curly kale from supermarkets. Chop ~400 g of savoy cabbage into wedges and ~400 g of broccoli into heads; boil each in 1.2 L Milli‑Q water (18.2 MQ) for ~15 min. Chop 360 g of curly kale and boil in ~1.6 L Milli‑Q water for 8 min. Drain all cooked vegetables at room temperature for 15 min, place in bags, freeze at –20 °C, freeze‑dry using a Coolsafe 110‑4 pro (ScanVac), then finely grind. Store the ground material in sealed bags in the dark at 4 °C inside a desiccator with silica‑gel beads.

substeps.instruction: Boil cabbage and broccoli (~400 g each) in 1.2 L Milli‑Q water for ~15 min.
Boil kale (360 g) in ~1.6 L Milli‑Q water for 8 min.
Drain cooked vegetables for 15 min at room temperature.
Freeze at –20 °C, then freeze‑dry (Coolsafe 110‑4 pro, ScanVac).
Store ground samples in sealed bags, dark, 4 °C, desiccator with silica‑gel beads.

steps.title: Extract zinc species via SPE
steps.instruction: Weigh two batches of 100 mg of the ground vegetable material. For each batch, perform solid‑phase extraction twice by adding 2 mL of either 200 mM ammonium nitrate buffer (pH 7.6) or 50 mM Tris/HCl buffer (pH 7.5) in plastic tubes, then sonicate at 20 % power for 2 min. Combine the two extracts from the same batch and vegetable type, and centrifuge the combined extract at 4000 g (relative centrifugal force) at 4 °C for 10 min.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 mL of chosen buffer (200 mM NH₄NO₃, pH 7.6 or 50 mM Tris/HCl, pH 7.5) to 100 mg sample in a plastic tube.
Sonicate at 20 % power for 2 min; repeat once (total two extractions).
Combine the two extracts for each batch/vegetable.
Centrifuge the combined extract at 4000 g, 4 °C, for 10 min.
